# Song of Songs Chapter 4 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 413v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/SNG_004_page_001.jpg

---

**4:1** Behold [hinnakh], you [are] beautiful [yafah], my-darling [ra'ayati]; behold, you [are] beautiful; your-eyes [einayikh] [are] doves [yonim] behind your-veil [le-tsammatekh]; your-hair [sa'arekh] [is] like-a-flock [ke-eder] of-goats [ha-izzim] that-stream-down [she-galeshu] from-Mount Gil'ad [Gilead].

**4:7** All-of-you [kullakh] [is] beautiful [yafah], my-darling, and-there-is-no [u-mum ein] blemish [mum] in-you.

**4:16** Awake [uri], O-north-wind [tsafon], and-come [u-vo'i], O-south [teiman]; blow-upon [hafichi] my-garden [ganni], [that] its-spices [besamav] may-flow [yizzelu]. Let-my-beloved [dodi] come [yavo] to-his-garden [le-ganno] and-eat [ve-yokhal] his-choice-fruits [peri megadav].

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1-7 — The wasf:** An Arabic literary form (descriptive love poem) praising the beloved's body from head to foot. The imagery is pastoral and agricultural — hair like goats, teeth like sheep, lips like scarlet thread — beauty described in terms of the land.

*— EMET*
